\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{せんたくもの} (sentakumono)}{せんたくもの (sentakumono)}]{\ja{せんたくもの} (sentakumono) — the laundry}

\label{lesson:JA-C102-sentakumono}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for a heated table, then the Japanese for heating.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{せんたくもの}}
\textbf{\ja{せんたくもの}} — \emph{sentakumono} — \textquotedblleft{}the laundry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{せんたくもの}} (\emph{sentakumono}) mixes the two layers: \emph{sentaku}, \textquotedblleft{}washing\textquotedblright{}, Sino-Japanese \emph{sen}, \textquotedblleft{}wash\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{taku}, \textquotedblleft{}rinse\textquotedblright{} (Middle Chinese \emph{draewk}), borrowed from Chinese, with native \emph{mono}, \textquotedblleft{}thing\textquotedblright{} (JMdict; Unihan, KANJIDIC2).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sentakumono}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sentakumono}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sentakumono}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Japanese for a heated table, then the Japanese for heating, then say \emph{sentakumono} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{せんざい} (senzai)}{せんざい (senzai)}]{\ja{せんざい} (senzai) — detergent}

\label{lesson:JA-C102-senzai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for heating, then the Japanese for the laundry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{せんざい}}
\textbf{\ja{せんざい}} — \emph{senzai} — \textquotedblleft{}detergent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{せんざい}} (\emph{senzai}) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are \emph{sen}, \textquotedblleft{}wash\textquotedblright{} and \emph{zai}, \textquotedblleft{}medicinal preparation\textquotedblright{} (Middle Chinese \emph{dzejH}) (Unihan, KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese after Baxter–Sagart).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{かま} (kama)}{かま (kama)}]{\ja{かま} (kama) — a rice pot}

\label{lesson:JA-C102-kama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for detergent, then the Japanese for a teacup.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{かま}}
\textbf{\ja{かま}} — \emph{kama} — \textquotedblleft{}a rice pot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{かま}} (\emph{kama}) is a native Japanese word, inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, and its older origin is not settled. Its kanji was attached to it later as a kun'yomi, a native reading given to a Chinese character (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).
\end{cousinweb}
